questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose ETH, because it offers a broad range of interesting courses. And Zurich has a really nice location close to the mountains - and in only a couple of hours of train ride you can be in Italy, France and Germany.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was super happy about my overall stay at ETH.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: ETH is very well organised, so I felt like I was well prepared. If sth was not clear, I wrote to the International Office of ETH - they are super helpful and write back quickly.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were several pre-arrival Zoom Meetings offered. And an Intro Day in the first week - which was super nice, because one gets to know a lot of fellow students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I got a room through WOKO. It was quite expensive (ca. 900CH per month) - but located right next to my faculty, in close proximity to the sports facilities of the ASVZ and the city centre.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: No meal plans - but a shared kitchen.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is more expensive than finding a room on the housing market. But one has to be lucky to find a place, where there take a person, that is only going to stay for one semester. I had the strong impression that most people prefer a more long-term tenant/flat mate.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The available spots are quite limited. And the rooms are in general very expensive.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I remember it was easy and straight-forward - one just has to follow the instructions that were given via mail and/or zoom meetings.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: If in doubt, I called or wrote to the responsible office. ETH staff was always very nice and could help very quickly with any issues.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I could do all the classes, except for one, where I did not fulfil the academic pre-requisites.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read the course description in the course book carefully and if in doubt write to the course coordinator.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some courses (especially the ones on a Master Level) were quite difficult and demanding - but that made it also more rewarding once one had „survived“ them :-)

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level is in general higher than at KU. In Copenhagen we for instance did statistical analyses with small data sets in Excel - at ETH we were confronted with much bigger and much more complex data that was analysed in R. Also, at ETH one gets only very little ECTS points for a course, although the work load is much higher.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I liked it a lot that we had to solve problems in the lectures - so one is not just passively sitting there and listening. And I also appreciated that in some courses we could work by ourselves; at my faculty in Copenhagen there is way too much group work and one never really gets the chance to develop own ideas.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Landscape Planning and Ecosystem Services (Lecture & GIS Exercise)
Atmosphere and Climate Seminar
Geographic Information Systems
GIST
Using R for Data Analysis and Graphics
Soil Physics
Atmospherical Chemistry
Geographic Data Processing with ArcGIS and Python
Language Course in French and Spanish

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed the Landscape Planning and Ecosystem Services because it was a nice combination of theory (lecture) and practice (GIS). And the professor is always open to discuss!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I was traveling a lot in Switzerland and even with the Halbtax this can become quite expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were even more expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sports is organised by ASVZ. Additionally, there are heaps of social events offered by the faculties.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I took two language classes at UZH to get to know people outside my academic field, which was super nice. And I tried a lot of different sports classes offered by the ASVZ!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Everything! Switzerland is a small but so diverse country - and most places are easily reached by public transport. I enjoyed hiking on the weekends a lot!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I am half German and have family in Switzerland - so that made adjustment to the local culture quite a lot easier.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to the Swiss fellow students sitting next to you in your course :-)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did find nothing in particular challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Swiss people are very outdoorsy and love their mountains!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Hiking boots.
Snow shoes.
Climbing gear.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I am super happy about all the things I learnt - it gave me a lot of good ideas for future projects!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting Copenhagen University to help me organise a ETH distance exam turned out to be the biggest challenge during my exchange.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
